newsitem.title: USA: Motorola trades off, outlook seen cautious.
newsitem.headline: Motorola trades off, outlook seen cautious.

text.p: Shares of Motorola Inc slipped on Tuesday despite the company's beating first quarter earnings estimates, as analysts said the company's outlook is positive but cautious.
"Expectations for improvement have been high, so you might be seeing some scaling back," said Robert Wilkes, an analyst for Brown Brothers Harriman.

Late Monday Motorola reported first quarter earnings of $0.53 a share including gains on the settlement of a patent suit and the sale of an investment. First quarter 1996 earnings were $0.63 a share, and the First Call consensus of analysts estimates, excluding the gains, was $0.45 a share.

Motorola said in a conference call with analysts that it expects a "modest" and "gradual" recovery in its key semiconductor sector. It said first quarter sales were lower, largely because of declines in the semiconductor sector.
"I think it's a relatively cautious outlook," said Lawrence Borgman, an analyst for Josephthal, Lyon & Ross.
Shares of Motorola traded off 1-1/4 at 59.
